comment: Every visual state of the in-game menu, declared once.
A state is a set of element overrides, applied through RmlUi's own API by
the offscreen renderer — the same SetProperty, SetClass and SetPseudoClass
calls the bridge and RmlUi itself make at runtime. It is never an edit to
the markup: matching markup strings would mean this file and the generator
both had to change whenever an element did, which is the duplication
'pseudo' sets a real pseudo-class, so a hover state renders the design's
own :hover rule rather than a second rule written for the screenshot.

A state names elements by id, or by position — 'controls-device-list>1' is the second option in the picker, whatever that console calls it, so one declaration renders on every console. scripts/menu_states.py refuses
a state whose elements are not in the document, and refuses two states that
render the same picture — declaring a state the design does not actually
draw differently is how three of these were the same image.
Adding a screen means adding entries here. Nothing else changes.

pause-menu.describes: the menu as it opens, before anything is chosen

controls.describes: the controls screen, with the pad and its callouts

picker-hovered.describes: the pointer on the closed picker, before it opens

picker-pressed.describes: the closed picker held down, before the list appears

picker-open.describes: the picker open, listing what the author included

picker-hover-selected.describes: the pointer on the option already in use

picker-hover-unselected.describes: the pointer on an option that is not in use

picker-keyboard.describes: an option reached by the arrow keys rather than the pointer

picker-option-pressed.describes: an option held down, before the button is released

picker-dragged-outside.describes: held down, pointer dragged off the list; releasing must not choose

control-focused.describes: a control selected for rebinding, ring and callout lit

capturing.describes: a button being captured, when CANCEL joins the action row
